title: Rival watch
method: The top five Republican 2028 contenders by the tracker’s national primary polling average (polls_2028.json), re-ranked each update. Vance, Rubio and DeSantis are ranked by the simple average across all opened polls (every poll reports them). Places 4–5 are ranked by each candidate’s mean share among only the opened polls that reported him (n shown), because most polls do not report minor candidates; Donald Trump (constitutionally barred) is excluded. Stance on each item is toward that rival, not toward Vance. Only items actually opened are listed; favorability is shown only where a poll was opened.

rivals.momentum: Rising in elite support: Fox News Digital (Nov 25) reports multiple House Republicans (Malliotakis, Stutzman, Gimenez, Haridopolos) pushing him to run and administration staff “about 50/50” between him and Vance; leads a new Arizona GOP poll 48.8–24.9 (Riparian Research, Nov 20–24) and the OnMessage early-state poll. Tucker Carlson is reported (Washington Examiner, Nov 24) to be preparing a third-party run only if Rubio is the nominee. National tracker average unchanged at 30.6 (Vance 34.1). Rubio has publicly dismissed 2028 talk.

favorability.note: From polls.json (same-poll comparison with Vance: 35 / 53). Not refreshed this update.

items.source: Fox News Digital (Elizabeth Elkind, Peter D’Abrosca)
items.summary: “Marco Rubio’s 2028 stock surges among House Republicans as Trump insiders split on Vance.” Rep. Malliotakis: “He’s the whole package”; Rep. Stutzman: “I am all in for Marco. He can be a unifier”; Rep. Gimenez says “a pretty good number” of colleagues would back him. An administration official: “if you asked him today, he’d say Rubio.” Also a tracker item.

Relayed the Washington Examiner report: “Tucker Carlson could enter the 2028 presidential race specifically to stop Marco Rubio from reaching the White House… preparing a potential third-party campaign if Rubio secures the Republican nomination.” Carlson called Rubio backers “neocons”; the threat is aimed at Rubio (critical toward him).

“Rubio’s been the hardcore MAGA Secretary of State that America needed and a bright point in the Trump administration… [he has] the fire” Vance lacks; calls a Carlson third-party bid a spoiler. Also a tracker item (mixed toward Vance).

Riparian Research survey of 1,045 Arizona registered Republicans (Nov 20–24, SMS text-to-web, MoE ±3.0, sponsor not stated): Rubio 48.8, Vance 24.9, DeSantis 14.2. Among Vance voters, 63.1% name Rubio as second choice. State poll; not in the national average. Relayed on X by Bill Postmus (@billpostmus, 153,323).

Rubio posted that he met Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani “to launch the eighth U.S.-Qatar Strategic Dialogue,” working “to advance shared economic and security priorities.” Vance met the prime minister separately the same day amid uncertainty over Iran (Washington Post, as relayed). The post drew 1,172 replies, a high reply-to-like ratio.

Poll relay: “CNN: Marco Rubio has surged and is now the front runner to be the 2028 Republican nominee,” Rubio 34% (+28 from a year ago), Vance 30% (−14). Source is Harry Enten’s Nov 22 ranking segment (Rubio 1st, Vance 2nd, DeSantis 3rd); an analyst’s summary, not a poll.

Former ambassador to Israel: Vance “made a foolish bet… in the Tucker crowd… Rubio, in contrast, represents true Republican conservative values.” Endorsed by Marc Thiessen (“Amen!”). Also a tracker item.
Tucker Carlson clip: “if you think Marco Rubio is better for this country than JD Vance, then you my friend, are a neocon.” Also a tracker item.
Relayed a HispanicsVote/Newsweek poll of Florida Hispanic Republican primary voters (Oct 14–18): Rubio 57, DeSantis 25, Vance 10 (73,320 views). Single-state subgroup; not in the national average.

rivals.role: Governor of Florida (term-limited; leaves office January 2027)
rivals.momentum: Steady: 14.2% in the new Arizona GOP poll (third; 26.8% as a second choice), tracker average unchanged at 12.9. Kalshi traders (Nov 24 relay) put his odds of running at 89%, highest in the field (a market price, not a poll). Axios book-project report (Nov 22) still the main positioning news.

items.summary: Market relay: “ODDS TO RUN FOR 2028 REPUBLICAN PRESIDENTIAL NOMINATION: Ron DeSantis: 89%, Ted Cruz: 84%, Glenn Youngkin: 73%, J.D. Vance: 72%… Marco Rubio: 63%… Stephen Miller: 20%… Donald Trump Jr.: 17%.” Prediction-market prices, not polls.

Scoop: DeSantis is quietly working on a book, two sources say, “a project likely to fuel speculation about his making another run for the White House.” Notes his AI-skeptic positions (an “AI Bill of Rights”) put him at odds with the Trump administration, a planned think tank (per NBC), and allies who doubt he will run again; he has not ruled out 2028.

Pro-Trump commentator relayed the Axios book report (“you know exactly what that means”) and said the GOP bench is “STACKED,” praising DeSantis, Rubio and Vance alike. Cites an Ipsos “excellent candidate” reading (Vance 34, Rubio 36, DeSantis 28) that was not opened.
Relayed commentator Shawn Farash urging Republicans not to discount DeSantis for 2028 over his 2024 run against Trump. Low engagement for the follower count.

rivals.momentum: Flat: average 5.3 (3 polls); not listed in the Arizona Riparian poll; Kalshi odds of running 17% (Nov 24 relay). No notable large-account 2028 items opened this update.

rivals.role: Secretary of Health and Human Services
rivals.momentum: Flat: average 4.0 (2 polls); Kalshi odds of running 22% (Nov 24 relay). No qualifying large-account 2028 items opened this update.

ranking_note: Nov 25, 2026: unchanged — no new national 2028 GOP primary poll. Vance 34.1, Rubio 30.6, DeSantis 12.9 (8 polls); Trump Jr. 5.3 (3 polls), RFK Jr. 4.0 (2 polls); Ted Cruz next (2.7, 3 polls). A new Arizona-only Riparian Research poll (Rubio 48.8, Vance 24.9, DeSantis 14.2) is not part of the national average. Stephen Miller is not listed in any opened poll. Nov 24, 2026: first ranking. Order unchanged at the top (Vance, Rubio, DeSantis). Adding the Rainey Center poll moved the averages to Vance 34.1 (33.9), Rubio 30.6 (31.6), DeSantis 12.9 (13.3). Trump Jr. (5.3%, 3 polls) and RFK Jr. (4.0%, 2 polls) fill places 4–5; Ted Cruz is next (2.7%, 3 polls). Stephen Miller is not listed in any opened poll.
